title: Initialization-mode verifier tail
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, and write $y$ as the paired encoding of Boolean words $x$ and the paired encoding of Boolean words $w$ and $r$. Let $R$ be a register assignment, $s$ a natural number, and $st$ a verifier-and-accumulator state. Suppose every register of $R$ is at most $(8W_N+8)(|y|+1)$, $R_A=2|x|+2$, $R_S=s$, and $R_T=0$; also suppose $s2|y|$ and $W_N(2s+1)w|$. Then the initialization-mode codec program, started at its verifier state $st$ with register values $R$, no answer yet, and input $y$, halts while satisfying the same register bound at every earlier time, and returns true exactly when the scan state passes the initialization checks, $R_{Pos}=1$, and either $N$ has no work tapes or the indicated bit of $w$ is true.
hypotheses_covered: A finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols
A register assignment bounded componentwise by $(8W_N+8)(|y|+1)$
caveat: The conclusion refers to the internal scan predicate and a particular bit of the encoded word; their tuple-level meanings are not supplied by the given informal definitions.
